newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister wants study of Rafale project.
newsitem.headline: French minister wants study of Rafale project.

text.p: France's Socialist Finance Minister has called for a "detailed reflection" on the Dassault Rafale warplane project, according to a set of parliamentary minutes.
Dominique Strauss-Kahn was quoted as telling a closed session of the parliamentary defence committee on Wednesday that study was necessary because of the high national defence bill.
"The defence budget, which is relatively high in France when compared to our partners, imposes a detailed reflection of such projects," official minutes quoted him as saying.
The minutes also suggested doubts over the previous centre-right government's tentative plan to order an extra 48 Rafale planes in addition to a firm order for 13.
"The 13 already in the construction phase don't pose a problem, but this is not so true regarding the timetable for the 48 others," Strauss-Kahn was quoted as saying.
The previous government, which the left defeated in a June 1 election, ordered 13 Rafale fighter planes from Dassault Aviation for the navy and the Air Force in May.
It had also said in February it was willing in principle to order 48 extra planes in return for a 10 percent price cut.
The Rafale programme is a venture between private Dassault Aviation, state-controlled electronics supplier Thomson-CSF and state engine maker Snecma.
The project was held up for about 18 months from November 1995 because of negotiations over the price cuts.
The Socialists said before taking office they would order an audit into the costs of the Rafale programme of some 20 billion francs. Each warplane costs about 300 million francs.
Defence is seen as one area likely to be targeted in budget savings designed to help France qualify for a single European currency by squeezing public deficits.
Strauss-Kahn told reporters after the committee hearing that he had asked all ministers to find savings in their budgets.
The previous government pledged to hold defence spending level for five years but froze 1.8 billion francs of the 1997 defence budget earlier this year as a precaution.
This year's original budget was around 191 billion francs.
